title: Return-to-Work Reduction of New Plan Months — Benefit Overpayment Accounts
content:
**Rule.** On Benefit Overpayment Accounts, a claimant back at work is expected to repay sooner. A new repayment plan is shortened according to the calendar days from the most recent weekly benefit payment on any of the claimant's Unemployment Benefit Claims to the handling date.

**Record read.** The most recent weekly benefit payment is the latest benefit payment entry on the ledgers of all the claimant's Unemployment Benefit Claims, dated by its issue date. Payments on every claim the claimant holds count, not only the claim the overpayment arose on.

| Calendar days since the most recent benefit payment | Months taken off the plan months |
|---|---|
| More than 365 (the long off-benefit days) | 3, the long return-to-work reduction |
| More than 90 (the short off-benefit days), up to 365 | 1, the short return-to-work reduction |
| 90 or fewer, or no benefit payment on record | None |

**Boundaries.** Exactly 365 days takes off 1 month and 366 days takes off 3; exactly 90 days takes off nothing and 91 days takes off 1.

**Hypothetical cases.**

| Most recent benefit payment issued | Handling date | Days | Months taken off |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10 January 2025 | 11 January 2026 | 366 | 3 |
| 10 January 2025 | 10 January 2026 | 365 | 1 |
| 1 March 2026 | 31 May 2026 | 91 | 1 |
| 1 March 2026 | 30 May 2026 | 90 | None |
